title: Flow
description: Version 2. The flow-tracer writes .reliability/flows/drafts/<id>.json; `audit record-flow <id>` checks it, replaces its ids with stable ones, stamps commit and fingerprint and writes .reliability/flows/<id>.json and its page. Facts only: failure scenarios and verdicts live in the audit store. Files without schemaVersion are version 1 (hops and boundaries) and are still read.

id.description: FLOW-<area>-<slug>, lower-case kebab; also the file name.

summary.description: One sentence in business terms, no class names.

fingerprint.description: Stamped by record-flow: {files: {path: sha256}, core: sha256 of the methods around every step's evidence}.

entries.description: Every entry point the flow crosses, in the order the flow reaches them. Segment A is the start.

trigger.description: Who starts it: Stripe, SQS care-invoice-events, cron 02:00, a user.

id.description: Any id in the draft; record-flow replaces it with P- and 8 hex of kind|name, the same in every flow.

name.description: Class, table, queue or system name.

steps.description: One arrow of the sequence diagram each, in the order they happen.

id.description: Any id in the draft; record-flow replaces it with S- and 8 hex of segment|kind|from|to|file|enclosing method, which survives a line shift.

to.description: Participant id; equal to from for TX_BEGIN, TX_COMMIT and TX_ROLLBACK.

label.description: What the arrow says: a method, a verb and path, a table action.

tx.description: Transaction id from transactions[] open at this step.

thread.description: request, listener, scheduler, or the executor participant id after a fork.

durable.description: Whether what this step creates survives a crash at the next step.

sync.description: false for a hand-off the caller does not wait for.

effectRef.description: {entrypointId, index}: the effects.jsonl effect this step came from, when there is one.

commit.description: Step id of its TX_COMMIT. Its evidence is the method's last statement, never a closing brace.

links.description: How one segment leads to the next.

toStep.description: null for MANUAL, where the loop closes outside the code, and for a rejected candidate.

key.description: Queue, topic, event type, provider or table that joins the two sides.

candidate.description: The atlas/links.jsonl row this decides, as `flow candidates` prints it. Required to reject one.

status.description: Computed by record-flow: the candidate's status, or AGENT when the scanner proposed none.

confidence.description: Computed by record-flow; a draft's value is replaced.

businessParts.description: Parts a product owner would recognise. Every DB_WRITE, MESSAGE_SEND, EXTERNAL_CALL, EVENT_PUBLISH and ASYNC_FORK step belongs to exactly one part.

ownsState.description: Tables or external objects the part creates or changes.

acknowledgements.description: One per entry: when its caller is told the work was accepted.

durableBefore.description: Whether every business effect the caller asked for is durable before this step.

stoppedAt.description: Calls deliberately not followed, with the reason.

candidatesUndecided.description: Computed by record-flow: candidate links out of the flow's entry points that no link decides. A STATIC one that leaves the flow undecided rejects the draft.

snippet.description: One line copied verbatim from file:line, with a real identifier in it; checked by verify-evidence.
